deep.reconstruction: This page has no mathematics. It is a handwritten list of ten names, each apparently written by a different person in a different pen and hand (green, black, dark blue, red, blue), so it looks like a sign-up or attendance sheet for a course or seminar. The names are Christine Voisin, Jean-Pierre Sagnet, Phrayab(?) Srithammavanh, François Razafintsalama, Thierry Pace, Jean-Claude Rodriguez, Henry Ester, Marcus Wanderley(?), Inés Azofeifa and Wilbert De Lima. Their varied origins (French, Laotian, Malagasy, Latin American) fit a Montpellier university audience in the 1970s–80s. A vertical line divides the sheet. At the top right, underlined, are two names or words separated by a heavy slash, roughly 'Thérond(?) / Contre(?)-Courrière(?)'. These may be names of other people, or a room or administrative note; the reading is uncertain. The previous page lists course topics: orientations, embeddings, H^i and Euler characteristic, coverings and π1, π1 versus Galois theory, coverings and complex functions, Weil conjectures. Taken together, this page is plausibly the participant list for a teaching course or seminar Grothendieck gave at Montpellier on topology and Galois theory leading to the Weil conjectures. The page serves no mathematical problem. The '68' at bottom left is the archive's folio number, not a date.

transcription_corrections: 'Marcus Wanderderly' is more plausibly 'Marcus Wanderley', a common Brazilian surname; the handwriting is ambiguous.
'Jean Claude RODRIGUEZ': the first name is written in cursive as 'Jean Claude'; the surname is in capitals with a dotted I ('RODRİGUEZ').
'Phrayab' is uncertain; the reading is plausible but could be 'Phrayab' or a similar Lao given name.
Top right: the reading 'Thérond / Contre-Courrière' is highly uncertain; the first word might be 'Théorie' or a surname.
'68' at bottom left is the archive folio number, not a date or content.
